chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlub who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
'When the servant says, "Allah knows," while he is lying, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Could you not find anyone other than Me to lie against?"'

key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — divine epithet emphasizing God's transcendence and authority
key_terms.عَلِمَ اللَّهُ: Allah knows — an invocation of divine omniscience, used here falsely as a witness to a lie
key_terms.كَاذِباً: Lying, being a liar — the person's actual state contradicts their invocation of God

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about falsely invoking God's name while lying?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against the grave sin of invoking God's knowledge as a false witness to one's lies — a practice sometimes called 'using God's name in vain' in Islamic ethics. The hadith portrays God directly rebuking the person who falsely claims divine knowledge as witness to their dishonesty. This narration was likely addressed to those who used the phrase 'God knows' (علم الله) as a rhetorical device to lend credibility to falsehoods, treating the invocation of divine omniscience as a verbal oath to strengthen deceptions.
